correctness.rationale: On the Hodge-good locus, Zou's Lemma 6.1 makes every \(E_i=R^{2i}f_*\mathcal O\) invertible with base change, and fibrewise Hodge-goodness makes the cup map \(E_1^{\otimes i}\to E_i\) nowhere vanishing, hence an isomorphism. Relative Frobenius gives \(F_S^*E_i\to E_i\), and because Frobenius is multiplicative, the cup-product square commutes, proving \(h_i=h_1^{\otimes i}\). Localizing an integral base turns this into the equation \(a^i\) for the \(i\)-th section, hence \(D_i=iD_1\). Zou's Lemma 6.2 and Theorem 6.7 then identify the common support with the non-Frobenius-split and infinite-height loci. The empty Frobenius-split case is explicitly excluded from the Cartier-divisor conclusion.

value.rationale: The source establishes only the open Frobenius-split locus from the top coherent Frobenius map. The new identity upgrades that set-theoretic information to a precise scheme-theoretic comparison across every even coherent degree: all local Hasse vanishing orders scale by exactly \(i\), and the top section carries an unavoidable \(n\)-fold thickening. Vanishing multiplicities of Hasse sections are independently known to encode meaningful geometry in K3 and Calabi--Yau-type settings, so identifying the exact multiplicity mechanism in the newly studied primitive-symplectic family setting is a natural structural refinement rather than a cosmetic reformulation.
